$comment: Generated from packages/core/src/errors.ts by tools/build-errors.mjs. Do not edit. Every code this library can produce, with the HTTP status it always carries. The status is a function of the code: one code never means two statuses.

ambiguous_subject.meaning: A share named more than one kind of subject at once.
ambiguous_subject.fix: Pass exactly one of `withUser` or `withOrg`. `minRole` is only meaningful with `withOrg`.

bad_cursor.meaning: A listing cursor was not one this library issued.
bad_cursor.fix: Pass back the `cursor` from the previous page unchanged, or omit it to start again.

bad_request.meaning: A request body did not parse.
bad_request.fix: Send valid JSON, or a form body, and a matching `content-type`.

credential_in_query.meaning: A share-link request carried a credential in the query string.
credential_in_query.fix: Put the password in a POST body. Query strings reach access logs, proxy logs and browser history.

credential_in_query_string.meaning: An authorized-read request carried a credential in the query string.
credential_in_query_string.fix: Same as `credential_in_query`, on the `/f` route. The two codes differ only by which route refused.

invalid_argument.meaning: An argument was outside what the operation accepts.
invalid_argument.fix: `reason` names the argument. It is safe to log and is not shown to an untrusted caller.

link_is_read_only.meaning: A share link was asked to carry a capability beyond `read`.
link_is_read_only.fix: Share with a named user or an org for anything other than reading. A link is a bearer token.

link_principal_cannot_list.meaning: A caller holding only a share link tried to list files.
link_principal_cannot_list.fix: A link grants one file. Listing needs an identity.

password_requires_link_subject.meaning: A password was set on a share that is not a link.
password_requires_link_subject.fix: Only a link has somewhere to prompt. Drop the password, or make it a link.

password_required.meaning: This share link has a password and none, or a wrong one, was supplied.
password_required.fix: Re-issue as a POST with `password` in the body. The response carries `WWW-Authenticate: FilelayerShare`.

forbidden.meaning: The caller has standing on the resource and may not do this particular thing. Narrower than it looks: it is used where a 404 would be less useful and leaks nothing, such as delegating more authority than you hold.
forbidden.fix: `reason` names the refusal for your logs.

not_found.meaning: The resource does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. These are deliberately the same answer: a permissions system that distinguishes them is a membership oracle.
not_found.fix: Nothing, from the caller. Check `reason` in your own logs to tell the two apart.

org_exists.meaning: An org with that external id already exists under a different owner.
org_exists.fix: Pick another id, or look the existing one up with `fl.ids.orgId()`.

retention_hold.meaning: A delete was refused because the file is under a retention hold.
retention_hold.fix: Wait for the hold to lapse. It cannot be lifted through this API, which is the point of a hold.

upload_not_received.meaning: A direct upload was completed but the object is not in the store.
upload_not_received.fix: The client never finished the PUT, or sent it elsewhere. Reserve again.

upload_size_mismatch.meaning: The object that arrived is not the size the upload was authorized for.
upload_size_mismatch.fix: Reserve again with the real size. The store should have refused this; if it did not, check that `content-length` is in the signed headers.

gone.meaning: The grant that would have allowed this has expired.
gone.fix: Ask the owner for a new link or a new grant.

upload_reservation_expired.meaning: The upload window closed before the bytes arrived.
upload_reservation_expired.fix: Reserve again. A reservation is deliberately short.

payload_too_large.meaning: A request body exceeded the limit for that route.
payload_too_large.fix: Send less. For file bytes, use a direct upload rather than a body.

range_not_satisfiable.meaning: A `Range` header parsed cleanly and cannot be satisfied by this object. An INVALID range is not this: it is ignored, and the whole object is served under a 200.
range_not_satisfiable.fix: The response carries `Content-Range: bytes */<size>`, which is the size you needed in order to ask a better question.

direct_upload_bad_max.meaning: `maxUploadBytes` was absent or not a positive integer.
direct_upload_bad_max.fix: Choose a ceiling. There is deliberately no default, because an exact pin to whatever the client asked for is not a bound.

direct_upload_bad_ttl.meaning: `ttlSeconds` for a direct upload was below 60.
direct_upload_bad_ttl.fix: Use at least 60. A shorter window fails real uploads on real networks.

direct_upload_not_acknowledged.meaning: Direct upload was configured without the verbatim acknowledgement string.
direct_upload_not_acknowledged.fix: Pass `DIRECT_UPLOAD_ACKNOWLEDGEMENT`. Handing the data path to the object store is a property you give up, not a setting you tune.

internal.meaning: Something failed that is not one of the above. This is the only code here that means a defect rather than a decision.

redirect_bad_ttl.fix: Use at least 1. Values above the maximum are clamped rather than refused.

redirect_not_acknowledged.meaning: Redirect delivery was configured without the verbatim acknowledgement string.
redirect_not_acknowledged.fix: Pass `REDIRECT_ACKNOWLEDGEMENT`. A redirect stays valid for its whole TTL after a grant is revoked.

storage_cannot_list.meaning: Orphan collection was asked of a storage adapter that cannot list objects.
storage_cannot_list.fix: Use an adapter that implements `list()`, or do not schedule `collectStorageOrphans()`.

direct_upload_not_enabled.meaning: Direct upload was requested on an instance that has not configured it.
direct_upload_not_enabled.fix: Configure `directUpload`, or use `upload()`, which sends bytes through your server and works on every adapter.

direct_upload_unsupported.meaning: The configured storage adapter cannot sign an upload.
direct_upload_unsupported.fix: `reason` names the provider. `FsStorage` can mint a local upload token instead; `MemoryStorage` cannot sign at all.
